newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Friday :
* A Jordanian soldier opened fire on a group of Israeli schoolgirls visiting shared land in the Jordan Valley, killing seven girls and wounding six others before he was captured.
* New York State regulators and Consolidated Edison agreed on a pact to restructure the utility, breaking it into pieces and giving rate cuts to large industrial users.
* Albanian authorities armed civilians in the capital of Tirana, as the government faced escalating violence and chaos there. At least 12 people have been killed and 50 wounded.
* News Analysis: An inquiry into Democratic fundraising during the recent U.S. presidential campaign has created tension among the country's top law enforcement officials.

* The White House and Congressional Republicans appear to be hitting an impasse over the budget, reviving the threat of another deadlock. Leaders of both political parties expressed pessismism about getting substantive talks started soon.
* An 18-year-old San Fernando Valley, Calif. man arrested in connection with the January 16 roadside killing of Bill Cosby's Ennis was charged with a single count of murder.
* Airline ticket prices have been increasing steadily for travelers, normally business people, who fly during the work week on short notice.
* A new report shows people have an innate sense of being either male or female, contradicting a case used to suggest sexual identity was not inborn.
